subject: Model pinning, rollback-hatch definition & customer comms — sync
messages:
From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 20 Sep 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Model pinning, rollback-hatch definition & customer comms — sync

Team —

Quick kickoff note: product wants a short, prescriptive definition of two things for the upcoming API/model phase:

1) "Pinning" / grace window: how long a customer can keep a pinned model version after we mark it deprecated before forced migration.
2) The "rollback hatch": clear, testable conditions that allow us to re-route traffic back to the older model during a failed rollout.

We need operational-level language (who toggles, metrics that trigger rollback, SLA/latency tolerances) and the proposed customer-facing comms cadence. I attached a starting draft (migration_plan_draft.pdf) and a customer notice template.

Asks for this thread:
- Engineering: define feasible pin duration options and what rollback metrics we can realistically instrument in the next 2 weeks (Karthik).
- Sales/CS: advise on customer impact/expectations for pin windows and whether we should offer a 30/60/90-day option at signup (Ben).
- Reliability/ops: outline how quickly we can flip traffic and what tests we need for the rollback hatch (Marissa / Marcus).

Timeline suggestion from product: decision by 2026-10-01 so we can bake comms into the Oct cutover cadence. If anyone needs a different timeline, call it out.

Notes: this is not a legal or pricing decision yet — just product/ops definition to inform later contract language.

Thanks,
Irene
Irene Choi
Senior PM, Model Lifecycle
Redwood Inference

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 20 Sep 2026 11:46:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Model pinning, rollback-hatch definition & customer comms — sync

Thanks Irene — good framing. A few practical thoughts from GTM: 

- Pin windows: customers will treat "pinning" like a contractual guarantee. Offering a 30/60/90-day selection is fine but we should require an explicit contract flag (so CS and legal can track). 30-day default keeps us flexible.
- Communication timing: for larger accounts (Acme-level), we should do a pre-notice + technical deep-dive + final cutover notice. For smaller customers a single opt-in notice 30 days prior is fine.
- For rollback hatch: customers will want clear SLAs around data consistency and request parity. We should be prepared with a short technical FAQ.

Suggested next steps:
1) Karthik: can you confirm whether the routing shim supports instantaneous flip (N minutes) vs. requires 15–60m to warm caches? We need a number to put in the customer comms.
2) Marissa: can you propose a soak/canary plan (percentages + gating metrics) for a safe rollout?
3) Product: pull the comms templates into a single doc we can iterate on with legal.

I can draft a two-line pre-notice for Acme that we can send once the pin window and rollback SLA are agreed.

-Ben
Ben Carter
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 20 Sep 2026 15:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Model pinning, rollback-hatch definition & customer comms — sync

Short engineering read:

- Pin window: technically we can enforce pin at routing level; retention of KV caches is the real cost. Options: 30-day (easy), 60-day (moderate), 90-day (high ops cost for high-traffic models). Recommend default 30-day with an enterprise opt-in for 90-day.
- Rollback hatch: we can implement a circuit that flips traffic back to the pinned model within ~2–5 minutes for live traffic, but the caveat is cache warm-up and KV/LLM state: request latency and token-level divergence may occur for first N requests. Metrics we can instrument immediately: error-rate delta, tail latency (p95/p99), and perplexity/response-drift via our eval hooks.
- Canary plan: promote 1% -> 5% -> 25% -> 100% over rolling windows (1h/2h/6h/24h) with automated rollback if p99 latency increases >30% or error-rate doubles. We can supply the metric thresholds as JSON and a small ops runbook.

Open technical asks:
1) Marissa/Marcus: can you confirm the staff ON-CALL for manual fallback during the 5–25% phases? We should have a playbook.
2) Product: do we allow customers to request pin extension via a self-serve flag in the Console, or must it be a sales contract? That affects instrumentation and billing.

I'll attach a short ops snippet to show gating thresholds (will upload to the Drive link).

-karthik
Karthik Iyer
Principal SW Eng — Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>

Date: Tue, 21 Sep 2026 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Model pinning, rollback-hatch definition & customer comms — sync

Thanks all — summary and owners below. I pulled the draft canary plan into the Drive link and attached a short playbook.

Decision / agreed defaults (proposed):
- Pin window default: 30 days. Enterprise opt-in: 90 days (requires contract flag). Owner: Ben (GTM) + Legal.
- Rollback hatch: automated flip with manual override. Flip time goal: <= 5 minutes (technical caveat: cache warm-up). Owner: Karthik (implementation) + Marcus (ops hardening).
- Canary rollout percentages & gates: 1% (1h), 5% (2h), 25% (6h), 100% (24h). Gating metrics: p99 latency delta (threshold: +30%), error-rate (2x baseline), response-drift score (pluggable threshold). Owner: Marissa (runbook) + Karthik (metrics).
- Customer comms: pre-notice (30 days) + detailed tech deep-dive for enterprise customers 7 days before. Owner: Ben + Irene (templates).

Open items and deadlines:
- Karthik: post the metrics JSON and confirm flip time estimate by 2026-09-24.
- Ben: confirm Acme comms cadence and whether contracts team needs a separate notice by 2026-09-27.
- Marcus/Marissa: verify on-call coverage and upload the runbook by 2026-09-28.
- Product (Irene): finalize the customer_notice_template.docx and share with Legal by 2026-09-29.

If there are objections to the defaults above, reply inline. If silent, we'll treat this as the working plan and capture it in the Oct cutover calendar.

Marissa
Marissa Cole
Head of Reliability
Redwood Inference
